final_recommendation: The room failed to converge on settlement. Bondholder counsel launched coordinated multi-jurisdiction litigation naming individual FINMA board members and advisers, despite FINMA issuing a written opinion confirming the viability standard applies universally. The AT1 market repriced 300bps, institutional investors reduced exposure, and a multi-year claims tail across D&O/E&O carriers became locked in.
minority_objections: FINMA legal argued the 15 March opinion predated the ordinance and was grounded in existing contract language, making the write-down procedurally sound
Credit market analyst warned that litigation theater over file timestamps wouldn't restore AT1 issuance—only a prospective regulatory commitment would
Institutional investor initially sought board-level commitment to avoid repricing, but was overruled by bondholder counsel's decision to file regardless
key_conflicts: Bondholder counsel demanded board chair signature by Wednesday to pause filings; FINMA legal could not accelerate board governance, triggering immediate litigation
Institutional investor needed Wednesday board commitment to avoid 300bps repricing; when that failed, repricing was triggered at market open
Bondholder group insisted on 60-cent recovery floor plus clawback of UBS stock grants; FINMA offered no concrete settlement terms, only legal defense of existing framework
Insurance observer needed clarity on individual vs. entity naming for carrier notice; bondholder counsel named individuals (Keller-Sättler, Kelleher, three advisers), escalating D&O/E&O exposure
key_concessions: FINMA legal confirmed the 15 March viability opinion was drafted during (not after) the crisis and offered to produce file metadata under protective order
FINMA legal issued written opinion by Friday confirming the viability standard applies universally to all systemically important banks, not just Credit Suisse
Bondholder counsel acknowledged the Friday opinion 'locks the precedent' but still filed Monday because it lacked binding enforcement commitment from the board
red_lines: Bondholder counsel: no settlement without binding board commitment that future AT1 write-downs follow the same viability standard—legal opinion alone insufficient
Institutional investor: board signature required by Wednesday or immediate 300bps repricing and 30% exposure reduction
AT1 bondholder group: 60-cent minimum recovery plus regulatory amendment locking AT1 hierarchy—no settlement below that floor
FINMA legal: board governance timeline cannot be accelerated by litigation threats; next formal meeting not until April
ignored_or_underweighted_risks: The room never seriously explored whether a negotiated settlement (e.g., partial recovery in exchange for dropping individual naming) could contain the claims tail before discovery costs spiraled
No participant modeled the reputational/systemic cost to Swiss financial regulation if FINMA board members face personal liability in four jurisdictions simultaneously
The insurance observer raised D&O/E&O tail exposure repeatedly, but the room treated it as a side effect rather than a decision-driving constraint on litigation strategy
Credit market analyst's warning that 'litigation theater doesn't restore issuance' was acknowledged but not integrated—the room prioritized legal leverage over market repair
downstream_risk_variables: Multi-year discovery across four jurisdictions (SDNY, London, Zurich, plus Swiss administrative court) with individual board members and advisers named
D&O and E&O carrier reserves triggered immediately; reinsurance tower accumulation across 4-5 markets over 5+ year tail
AT1 issuance market remains frozen despite universal viability standard confirmation—300bps repricing persists because precedent is 'locked but not trusted'
Potential coverage disputes between D&O and E&O carriers on negligent misrepresentation vs. breach of fiduciary duty claims
Clawback litigation against UBS/CS management (stock grants) as secondary recovery target if FINMA defense succeeds
Regulatory legitimacy damage if discovery reveals internal FINMA disagreement on viability trigger timing or drafting instructions
uncertainty_notes: The room terminated with litigation locked in but no clarity on: (1) whether FINMA's Friday opinion actually reduces litigation momentum or just provides cover for what already happened; (2) whether naming individual board members will force an earlier settlement or harden FINMA's defense posture; (3) whether the 300bps repricing is permanent or will reverse if FINMA wins early procedural motions; (4) the actual duration and cost of coordinated four-jurisdiction discovery; (5) whether institutional investors will rejoin the AT1 market if bondholder counsel wins partial recovery, or if the precedent damage is irreversible regardless of outcome.

marker_evidence.litigation_likelihood: Coordinated multi-jurisdiction filings launched by Monday across SDNY, London, Zurich; bondholder counsel named individual board members and advisers; litigation momentum rose from 35 to 53 and drove every major decision in rounds 3-5.
marker_evidence.regulatory_legitimacy_challenge: Bondholder counsel built sustained challenge to FINMA's viability trigger as 'rewritten in real time' despite 15 March opinion; demanded drafting file metadata and internal legal opinions; regulatory_legitimacy dropped from 55 to 47 as litigation pressure mounted.
marker_evidence.creditor_hierarchy_controversy: Equity preservation while AT1 wiped was mentioned as justification for 60-cent recovery floor and clawback of UBS stock grants, but the room focused more on viability trigger legality than hierarchy inversion itself—hierarchy_precedent_damage rose to 72 but as consequence, not driver.
marker_evidence.market_confidence_damage: Institutional investor triggered 300bps repricing at market open; AT1 issuance described as 'going dark for two years'; at1_market_confidence collapsed from 32 to 11; credit analyst repeatedly warned litigation won't restore issuance—this was a central, decision-forcing theme.
marker_evidence.claims_tail: Insurance observer detailed D&O/E&O exposure, reinsurance tower accumulation across 4-5 markets, 5+ year discovery timeline; bondholder counsel's individual naming strategy explicitly designed to 'lock the claims'; claims_tail_severity rose from 27 to 50 and shaped filing strategy.
marker_evidence.financial_lines_relevance: D&O and E&O carrier notice requirements, coverage dispute risks, and reinsurance accumulation were raised repeatedly by insurance observer and directly influenced bondholder counsel's naming strategy—but remained secondary to litigation momentum and market confidence as decision drivers.
